{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_030f7016c46d460c9742290d","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# T4b Deletion Lifecycle — Receiver-Side Output Management\n2\t\n3\t**Bead:** `bf-1yk1`  \n4\t**Plan reference:** §12 T4, E10, E15  \n5\t**Phase:** Phase 4 (Large-file machinery)\n6\t\n7\t## Overview\n8\t\n9\tT4b addresses **receiver-side plaintext residue** — the complete decoded file staged in OPFS during reception. Unlike sender-side staging (T4a), the receiver's output **is the deliverable** and cannot be deleted immediately after the transfer completes.\n10\t\n11\tFor the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds), indefinite plaintext storage in browser storage is a security exposure. OPFS is not encrypted at rest, and the OS/browser may retain data beyond the application's control.\n12\t\n13\t## The Deletion Lifecycle\n14\t\n15\tThe receiver's output file MUST follow this lifecycle:\n16\t\n17\t### 1. Automatic Deletion After Successful Export\n18\tWhen the user successfully exports the completed file via `share()` or `save()`:\n19\t- **Delete the OPFS artefact immediately** after the export succeeds\n20\t- Clear all associated metadata from OPFS\n21\t- Do NOT wait for tab close or browser exit — the file is no longer needed\n22\t\n23\t### 2. Startup Reaping of Orphaned Outputs\n24\tOn application startup:\n25\t- Scan OPFS for output artefacts that were not cleaned up (crashes, tab kills, navigation away)\n26\t- Reap orphans older than a threshold (e.g., 24 hours) or offer user choice\n27\t- Provide a UI indicator when orphaned files exist\n28\t- Allow user to recover or delete orphaned files\n29\t\n30\t### 3. Warning Before Keeping Partial Artefacts\n31\tWhen keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15):\n32\t- **E10 (OPFS quota exhausted):** Export partial file + missing manifest\n33\t  - Show explicit warning: \"This is an incomplete file. It will be stored until you delete it.\"\n34\t  - Require user acknowledgment before keeping the partial artefact\n35\t  - Mark the artefact clearly as \"partial\" in the UI\n36\t- **E15 (Decompression failure):** Keep compressed artefact\n37\t  - Show explicit warning: \"Decompression failed. The raw data will be stored until you delete it.\"\n38\t  - Require user acknowledgment before keeping the artefact\n39\t  - Mark the artefact clearly as \"compressed/raw\" in the UI\n40\t\n41\t### 4. User-Visible Delete Control\n42\tProvide in-band deletion controls:\n43\t- **Files list screen:** Show all stored output files (complete, partial, compressed)\n44\t- **Per-file actions:** Delete button for each artefact\n45\t- **Bulk actions:** \"Delete all\" option\n46\t- **Clear indication:** Show file size, type, and age to help users decide\n47\t- **Confirmation:** Require confirmation for deletion (non-recoverable)\n48\t\n49\t## Implementation Requirements\n50\t\n51\t### Storage Layer (`src/platform/storage.ts`)\n52\t\n53\t```typescript\n54\tinterface OutputArtefact {\n55\t  id: string;              // Unique identifier (e.g., streamId-based)\n56\t  filename: string;        // Sanitised original filename\n57\t  mimeType: string;        // Declared MIME type\n58\t  size: number;           // Actual size in OPFS\n59\t  status: 'complete' | 'partial' | 'compressed';\n60\t  createdAt: number;      // Timestamp when created\n61\t  streamId?: number;      // Associated stream ID for debugging\n62\t  missingBlocks?: number[]; // For partial artefacts (E10)\n63\t}\n64\t\n65\tinterface StorageManager {\n66\t  // Write completed file to OPFS\n67\t  writeOutput(streamId: number, filename: string, data: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;\n68\t  \n69\t  // Delete after successful export\n70\t  deleteOutput(streamId: number): Promise<void>;\n71\t  \n72\t  // Startup reap of orphans\n73\t  reapOrphans(maxAge?: number): Promise<OutputArtefact[]>;\n74\t  \n75\t  // List all artefacts for UI\n76\t  listOutputs(): Promise<OutputArtefact[]>;\n77\t  \n78\t  // Keep partial artefact with warning\n79\t  keepPartial(streamId: number, partialData: Uint8Array, missing: number[]): Promise<void>;\n80\t}\n81\t```\n82\t\n83\t### Key Implementation Points\n84\t\n85\t1. **Naming convention:** OPFS filenames should be obfuscated (not the original filename) to avoid leaking file metadata. Use a streamId-based naming scheme.\n86\t\n87\t2. **Metadata persistence:** Maintain a small manifest mapping streamId → artefact metadata. This manifest lives in OPFS alongside the files.\n88\t\n89\t3. **Delete timing:** \n90\t   - Delete immediately after successful `share()` or `save()` resolves\n91\t   - Do NOT wait for tab close (unreliable)\n92\t   - Do NOT wait for manual cleanup (security exposure)\n93\t\n94\t4. **Reap strategy:**\n95\t   - On startup, read the manifest\n96\t   - For each artefact, check `createdAt` against current time\n97\t   - Auto-reap artefacts older than threshold (default: 24 hours)\n98\t   - Show UI notification for artefacts below threshold\n99\t\n100\t5. **Partial artefact handling:**\n101\t   - Store with the `OutputArtefact.status = 'partial'` flag\n102\t   - Include `missingBlocks` array for potential future resume\n103\t   - UI should show clearly: \"Incomplete file (X of Y blocks received)\"\n104\t\n105\t## Integration with Edge Cases\n106\t\n107\t### E10: OPFS Quota Exhausted\n108\t```typescript\n109\t// When quota exhaustion occurs\n110\tasync function handleQuotaExhausted(completedBlocks: Map<number, Uint8Array>, missing: number[]) {\n111\t  // Export partial file + manifest of missing blocks\n112\t  const partialData = concatenateBlocks(completedBlocks);\n113\t  \n114\t  // Show warning to user\n115\t  const acknowledged = await showWarning(\n116\t    \"Out of space. Partial file will be stored until you delete it.\"\n117\t  );\n118\t  \n119\t  if (acknowledged) {\n120\t    await storage.keepPartial(streamId, partialData, missing);\n121\t    // Offer export of partial file + missing manifest\n122\t    exportPartialFile(partialData, missing);\n123\t  }\n124\t}\n125\t```\n126\t\n127\t### E15: Decompression Failure\n128\t```typescript\n129\t// When decompression fails at the end\n130\tasync function handleDecompressionFailure(compressedData: Uint8Array) {\n131\t  // Show warning to user\n132\t  const acknowledged = await showWarning(\n133\t    \"Decompression failed. Raw data will be stored until you delete it.\"\n134\t  );\n135\t  \n136\t  if (acknowledged) {\n137\t    await storage.keepCompressed(streamId, compressedData);\n138\t    // Offer export of compressed artefact\n139\t    exportCompressedFile(compressedData);\n140\t  }\n141\t}\n142\t```\n143\t\n144\t## Testing Requirements\n145\t\n146\t### Integration Tests\n147\t\n148\t1. **Successful receiveFileSuccessfully();\n153\t     await exportViaShare();\n154\t     const outputs = await storage.listOutputs();\n155\t     expect(outputs).toHaveLength(0);\n156\t   });\n157\t   ```\n158\t\n159\t2. **Orphan reaping:**\n160\t   ```typescript\n161\t   // Assert: reap deletes orphans\n162\t   await test('Reap deletes orphans', async () => {\n163\t     await await storage.reapOrphans();\n169\t     expect(orphans).toHaveLength(1);\n170\t     expect(orphors[0].status).toBe('complete');\n171\t     \n172\t     // After reap threshold expires\n173\t     await storage.reapOrphans(threshold);\n174\t     const remaining = await storage.listOutputs();\n175\t     expect(remaining).toHaveLength(0);\n176\t   });\n177\t   ```\n178\t\n179\t3. **Partial artefact   });\n188\t   ```\n189\t\n190\t4. **UI delete control:**\n191\t   ```typescript\n192\t   // Assert: UI has delete control\n193\t   await test('UI has delete control', async () => {\n194\t     await Overview\\n8\\t\\n9\\tT4b addresses **receiver-side plaintext residue** — the complete decoded file staged in OPFS during reception. Unlike sender-side staging (T4a), the receiver's output **is the deliverable** and cannot be deleted immediately after the transfer completes.\\n10\\t\\n11\\tFor the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds), indefinite plaintext storage in browser storage is a security exposure. OPFS is not encrypted at rest, and the OS/browser may retain data beyond the application's control.\\n12\\t\\n13\\t## The Deletion Lifecycle\\n14\\t\\n15\\tThe receiver's output file MUST follow this lifecycle:\\n16\\t\\n17\\t### 1. Automatic Deletion After Successful Export\\n18\\tWhen the user successfully exports the completed file via `share()` or `save()`:\\n19\\t- **Delete the OPFS artefact immediately** after the export succeeds\\n20\\t- Clear all associated metadata from OPFS\\n21\\t- Do NOT wait for tab close or browser exit — the file is no longer needed\\n22\\t\\n23\\t### 2. Startup Reaping of Orphaned Outputs\\n24\\tOn application startup:\\n25\\t- Scan OPFS for output artefacts that were not cleaned up (crashes, tab kills, navigation away)\\n26\\t- Reap orphans older than a threshold (e.g., 24 hours) or offer user choice\\n27\\t- Provide a UI indicator when orphaned files exist\\n28\\t- Allow user to recover or delete orphaned files\\n29\\t\\n30\\t### 3. T4b Deletion Lifecycle — Receiver-Side Output Management\\n2\\t\\n3\\t**Bead:** `bf-1yk1`  \\n4\\t**Plan reference:** §12 T4, E10, E15  \\n5\\t**Phase:** Phase 4 (Large-file machinery)\\n6\\t\\n7\\t## Overview\\n8\\t\\n9\\tT4b addresses **receiver-side plaintext residue** — the complete decoded file staged in OPFS during reception. Unlike sender-side staging (T4a), the receiver's output **is the deliverable** and cannot be deleted immediately after the transfer completes.\\n10\\t\\n11\\tFor the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds), indefinite plaintext storage in browser storage is a security exposure. OPFS is not encrypted at rest, and the OS/browser may retain data beyond the application's control.\\n12\\t\\n13\\t## The Deletion Lifecycle\\n14\\t\\n15\\tThe receiver's output file MUST follow this lifecycle:\\n16\\t\\n17\\t### 1. Automatic Deletion After Successful Export\\n18\\tWhen the user successfully exports the completed file via `share()` or `save()`:\\n19\\t- **Delete the OPFS artefact immediately** after the export succeeds\\n20\\t- Clear all associated metadata from OPFS\\n21\\t- Do NOT wait for tab close or browser exit — the file is no longer needed\\n22\\t\\n23\\t### 2. Startup Reaping of Orphaned Outputs\\n24\\tOn application startup:\\n25\\t- Scan OPFS for output artefacts that were not cleaned up (crashes, tab kills, navigation away)\\n26\\t- Reap orphans older than a threshold (e.g., 24 hours) or offer user choice\\n27\\t- Provide a UI indicator when orphaned files exist\\n28\\t- Allow user to recover or delete orphaned files\\n29\\t\\n30\\t### 3. Warning Before Keeping Partial Artefacts\\n31\\tWhen keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15):\\n32\\t- **E10 (OPFS quota exhausted):** Export partial file + missing manifest\\n33\\t  - Show explicit warning: \\\"This is an incomplete file. It will be stored until you delete it.\\\"\\n34\\t  - Require user acknowledgment before keeping the partial artefact\\n35\\t  - Mark the artefact clearly as \\\"partial\\\" in the UI\\n36\\t- **E15 (Decompression failure):** Keep compressed artefact\\n37\\t  - Show explicit warning: \\\"Decompression failed. The raw data will be stored until you delete it.\\\"\\n38\\t  - Require user acknowledgment before keeping the artefact\\n39\\t  - Mark the artefact clearly as \\\"compressed/raw\\\" in the UI\\n40\\t\\n41\\t### 4. User-Visible Delete Control\\n42\\tProvide in-band deletion controls:\\n43\\t- **Files list screen:** Show all stored output files (complete, partial, compressed)\\n44\\t- **Per-file actions:** Delete button for each artefact\\n45\\t- **Bulk actions:** \\\"Delete all\\\" option\\n46\\t- **Clear indication:** Show file size, type, and age to help users decide\\n47\\t- **Confirmation:** Require confirmation for deletion (non-recoverable)\\n48\\t\\n49\\t## Implementation Requirements\\n50\\t\\n51\\t### Storage Layer (`src/platform/storage.ts`)\\n52\\t\\n53\\t```typescript\\n54\\tinterface OutputArtefact {\\n55\\t  id: string;              // Unique identifier (e.g., streamId-based)\\n56\\t  filename: string;        // Sanitised original filename\\n57\\t  mimeType: string;        // Declared MIME type\\n58\\t  size: number;           // Actual size in OPFS\\n59\\t  status: 'complete' | 'partial' | 'compressed';\\n60\\t  createdAt: number;      // Timestamp when created\\n61\\t  streamId?: number;      // Associated stream ID for debugging\\n62\\t  missingBlocks?: number[]; // For partial artefacts (E10)\\n63\\t}\\n64\\t\\n65\\tinterface StorageManager {\\n66\\t  // Write completed file to OPFS\\n67\\t  writeOutput(streamId: number, filename: string, data: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;\\n68\\t  \\n69\\t  // Delete after successful export\\n70\\t  deleteOutput(streamId: number): Promise<void>;\\n71\\t  \\n72\\t  // Startup reap of orphans\\n73\\t  reapOrphans(maxAge?: number): Promise<OutputArtefact[]>;\\n74\\t  \\n75\\t  // List all artefacts for UI\\n76\\t  listOutputs(): Promise<OutputArtefact[]>;\\n77\\t  \\n78\\t  // Keep partial artefact with warning\\n79\\t  keepPartial(streamId: number, partialData: Uint8Array, missing: number[]): Promise<void>;\\n80\\t}\\n81\\t```\\n82\\t\\n83\\t### Key Implementation Points\\n84\\t\\n85\\t1. **Naming convention:** OPFS filenames should be obfuscated (not the original filename) to avoid leaking file metadata. Use a streamId-based naming scheme.\\n86\\t\\n87\\t2. **Metadata persistence:** Maintain a small manifest mapping streamId → artefact metadata. This manifest lives in OPFS alongside the files.\\n88\\t\\n89\\t3. **Delete timing:** \\n90\\t   - Delete immediately after successful `share()` or `save()` resolves\\n91\\t   - Do NOT wait for tab close (unreliable)\\n92\\t   - Do NOT wait for manual cleanup (security exposure)\\n93\\t\\n94\\t4. **Reap strategy:**\\n95\\t   - On startup, read the manifest\\n96\\t   - For each artefact, check `createdAt` against current time\\n97\\t   - Auto-reap artefacts older than threshold (default: 24 hours)\\n98\\t   - Show UI notification for artefacts below threshold\\n99\\t\\n100\\t5. **Partial artefact handling:**\\n101\\t   - Store with the `OutputArtefact.status = 'partial'` flag\\n102\\t   - Include `missingBlocks` array for potential future resume\\n103\\t   - UI should show clearly: \\\"Incomplete file (X of Y blocks received)\\\"\\n104\\t\\n105\\t## Integration with Edge Cases\\n106\\t\\n107\\t### E10: OPFS Quota Exhausted\\n108\\t```typescript\\n109\\t// When quota exhaustion occurs\\n110\\tasync function handleQuotaExhausted(completedBlocks: Map<number, Uint8Array>, missing: number[]) {\\n111\\t  // Export partial file + manifest of missing blocks\\n112\\t  const partialData = concatenateBlocks(completedBlocks);\\n113\\t  \\n114\\t  // Show warning to user\\n115\\t  const acknowledged = await showWarning(\\n116\\t    \\\"Out of space. of compressed artefact\\n139\\t    exportCompressedFile(compressedData);\\n140\\t  }\\n141\\t}\\n142\\t```\\n143\\t\\n144\\t## Testing Requirements\\n145\\t\\n146\\t### Integration is being retried\n212\t   * @returns true if livelock was detected, false otherwise\n213\t   */\n214\t  recordRetry(blockIndex: number): boolean {\n215\t    const now = Date.now();\n216\t\n217\t    // Clean up old failures outside the window\n218\t    this.failures = this.failures.filter(\n219\t      f => now - f.timestamp < this.config.FAILURE_WINDOW\n220\t    );\n221\t\n222\t    // Update (this.failures.length >= this.config.MAX_TOTAL_FAILURES) {\n236\t      // Already at total limit, increment and return livelock\n237\t      this.perBlockRetries.set(blockIndex, currentCount + 1);\n238\t      this.failures.push({ blockIndex, timestamp: now });\n239\t      return true;\n240\t    }\n241\t\n242\t    // Under limits, increment and record\n243\t    this.perBlockRetries.set(blockIndex, currentCount + 1);\n244\t    this.failures.push({ blockIndex, timestamp: now });\n245\t\n246\t    return false; // No livelock\n247\t  }\n248\t\n249\t  /**\n250\t @param blockIndex - The block index to check\n261\t   * @returns true if the block has exceeded its limit\n262\t   */\n263\t  hasExceededLimit(blockIndex: number): boolean {\n264\t    const count = this.perBlockRetries.get(blockIndex) || 0;\n265\t    return count >= this.config.MAX_RETRIES_PER_BLOCK;\n266\t  }\n267\t\n268\t  /**\n269\t   * Reset retry tracking for a specific block after successful operation\n270\t   * @param blockIndex - The block index to reset\n271\t   */\n272\t  resetBlock(blockIndex: number): void {\n273\t    this.perBlockRetries.delete(blockIndex);\n274\t    // Also remove failures for this block\n275\t    this.failures = this.failures.filter(f => f.blockIndex !== blockIndex);\n276\t  }\n277\t\n278\t  /**\n279\t   * Reset all tracking (e.g., after manifest Everything else is explanation.\n29\t\n30\t---\n31\t\n32\t## 1. Objective\n33\t\n34\t> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n35\t> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n36\t> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n37\t>\n38\t> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n39\t\n40\t- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n41\t  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n42\t- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n43\t- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n44\t- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n45\t\n46\t### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n47\t\n48\tMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\n49\tdesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\n50\tBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n51\t\n52\t| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n53\t|---|---|---|---|\n54\t| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n55\t| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n56\t| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n57\t| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n58\t| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n59\t\n60\t> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n61\t> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n62\t> one would overstate throughput.\n63\t\n64\t**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\n65\tand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n66\t\n67\t1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n68\t2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n69\t3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n70\t   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n71\t\n72\t---\n73\t\n74\t## 2. Glossary\n75\t\n76\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n77\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\n78\tplan they mean exactly this:\n79\t\n80\t| Term | Meaning here |\n81\t|---|---|\n82\t| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n83\t| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n84\t| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n85\t| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n86\t| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n87\t| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n88\t| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n89\t| **Beacon** | A special **packet** carrying file-level metadata instead of payload. Beacon packets are encoded into tiles and mixed into display frames by the frame mixer (D17, §7.2). |\n90\t| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n91\t| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n92\t| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n93\t| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n94\t| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n95\t| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n96\t| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n97\t| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n98\t| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n99\t\n100\t---\n101\t\n102\t## 3. What multi-gigabyte breaks, and the fix\n103\t\n104\tFour assumptions in the pre-multi-GB design do not survive contact with a 4 GB file.\n105\t\n106\t### 3.1 The fountain decoder does not scale — in TIME, not memory\n107\t\n108\tThis is the correction the plan review surfaced, and it matters because the first\n109\tversion of this section got it half right.\n110\t\n111\tD5 chose an LT code with a **Gaussian elimination** decoder, verified at\n112\t[`sim/`](../research/sim/). GE costs O(K²) in *memory* and O(K³) in *bit operations*.\n113\tThe original block-layer decision sized K from the memory term alone and concluded 4 MB\n114\tblocks (K = 16,384) were fine because the coefficient matrix is only 32 MB.\n115\t\n116\t**The memory term was never the binding constraint. Time is.**\n117\t\n118\tEach arriving packet is reduced against up to `rank` stored pivot rows; each row\n119\toperation XORs the coefficient mask (K/8 bytes) *and* the payload (L bytes). Reaching\n120\tfull rank costs `W = 2 · (K²/2) · (K/8 + L) = K² · (K/8 + L)` bytes of memory traffic,\n121\tand the block only lasts `K·L / R` seconds at wire rate R — so the decoder must\n122\t**sustain**:\n123\t\n124\t```\n125\trequired = W / (K·L/R) = K · (K/8 + L) · R / L    bytes/sec\n126\t```\n127\t\n128\t> The leading factor is **1, not 2** — the 2 and the /2 in `W` cancel. A previous\n129\t> revision of this section printed `2 · K · (K/8 + L) · R / L` and was 2× too\n130\t> pessimistic in every derived figure. Gate **G7** now diffs this section against the\n131\t> model so the class of error cannot recur.\n132\t\n133\tAll figures below are emitted by\n134\t[`sim/ge_cost_model.py`](../research/sim/ge_cost_model.py) — this section quotes the\n135\tmodel rather than reasoning beside it. **All rows at Stage 1 (R = 30 KB/s)**, so they\n136\tare comparable:\n137\t\n138\t| K | L | Block | Matrix | Work/block | Sustained need | |\n139\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n140\t| 1,000 | 1260 | 1.2 MB | 122.1 KB | 1.3 GB | 33.8 MB/s | research baseline |\n141\t| 1,500 | 1260 | 1.8 MB | 274.7 KB | 3.0 GB | 52.9 MB/s | research partitioning ceiling |\n142\t| 4,000 | 1260 | 4.8 MB | 1.9 MB | 26.2 GB | 171.6 MB/s | research called this **\"too slow\"** |\n143\t| **16,384** | **256** | **4.0 MB** | **32.0 MB** | **576.0 GB** | **4.5 GB/s** | **23× over budget** |\n144\t\n145\tThe plan's own evidence base\n146\t([`fountain-codes-and-protocol.md`](../research/fountain-codes-and-protocol.md) §2.6)\n147\tstates: *\"Cost scales as K², so it must be bounded. At K = 4000 the decode work is ~16×\n148\tthat of K = 1000 (~6 GB of XOR) — too slow\"* and recommends *\"source-block partitioning\n149\tabove K ≈ 1500\"*. **K = 16,384 was 11× past that ceiling.**\n150\t\n151\tIt was worse than a simple overshoot: shrinking L to 256 B to fit small tiles made the\n152\tmask term (K/8 = 2048 B) dominate the payload term (256 B) by 8×, so the decode problem\n153\tgot *harder* as a side effect of a decision made for a different reason.\n154\t\n155\t**Two further findings from the model:**\n156\t\n157\t- **A faster wire rate makes decode harder** — same work, less time to do it. So K MUST\n158\t  be sized for the *fastest* stage we intend to reach (Stage 3, 106 KB/s), not the\n159\t  slowest. This is counterintuitive and is why the original error was easy to make.\n160\t- **The sender's cost was unbudgeted too.** §6.3.1 counted QR encode and render but not\n161\t  the fountain XOR. At uncapped harmonic degree and K = 16,384 that is 398 KB of XOR\n162\t  per packet — **91.8 MB/s** at the old 225 packets/s (1 packet/tile), or **183.6 MB/s**\n163\t  at the adopted 450 packets/s (2 packets/tile at R2 nominal), on top of everything\n164\t  else. Hence D25.\n165\t\n166\t**Fix — D19:** K = **768**, L = **256 B**, block = **192.0 KB**.\n167\t\n168\t| | Was | Now |\n169\t|---|---|---|\n170\t| K | 16,384 | **768** |\n171\t| L | 256 B | **256 B** (unchanged — see §3.1.1) |\n172\t| Block | 4 MB | **192.0 KB** |\n173\t| GE matrix | 32.0 MB | **72.0 KB** |\n174\t| Block-layer working set | ~36 MB (claimed) | **264.0 KB** |\n175\t| Sustained need @ Stage 3 | 14.9 GB/s | **114.6 MB/s** |\n176\t\n177\t*Both \"sustained need\" figures are at Stage 3, so they compare like with like. The\n178\t4.5 GB/s in the table above is the same design at Stage 1.*\n179\t\n180\t**K_max at Stage 3 is 1152.** We adopt **768** deliberately below the ceiling —\n181\tD26 requires the sender to assume the weaker receiver, and the 200 MB/s budget is\n182\titself an unmeasured estimate (§18 R1). Margin at Stage 3: **1.74×**.\n183\t\n184\t| K | Block | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 | |\n185\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n186\t| 512 | 128.0 KB | 19.7 MB/s | 39.3 MB/s | 69.5 MB/s | 2.88× margin |\n187\t| **768** | **192.0 KB** | **32.4 MB/s** | **64.9 MB/s** | **114.6 MB/s** | **adopted, 1.74× margin** |\n188\t| 1024 | 256.0 KB | 47.2 MB/s | 94.4 MB/s | 166.7 MB/s | 1.20× margin |\n189\t| 1152 | 288.0 KB | 55.3 MB/s | 110.6 MB/s | 195.4 MB/s | 1.02× — the ceiling |\n190\t| 1536 | 384.0 KB | 82.6 MB/s | 165.2 MB/s | 291.8 MB/s | 1.5× **over** at Stage 3 |\n191\t\n192\t### 3.1.1 L is set by the *conservative* ladder rung, not the nominal one\n193\t\n194\tA revision of this plan briefly set L = 507 B (\"one packet per v15 tile\") and broke\n195\tD16's ladder. That destroys the ladder's one load-bearing property: *a mis-guessed profile\n199\tyields zero; a ladder always yields something.*\n200\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"call_3288fc39ddb643efbb686cf2","session_id":"2b964a3b-8195-41b5-b4db-1591503d2742","uuid":"28918e8b-89a0-449f-9ffe-d773a7554de6","timestamp":"2026-08-02T23:22:25.697Z","subagent_type":"Explore","task_description":"Explore receiver artefact handling"}
